messages:
Juno (support): Heads-up — ACME Integrations reported a reproducible JSON parse failure when consuming our streaming JSON (json_mode). They get "Unterminated string" from their parser. Sample concatenated chunks from their capture below (they're using stream=true):

Juno (support): ```chunk A:
{"id":123,"path":"C:\\Users\\alice\\Docu\
```
```chunk B:
ments\\notes":"Line1\nLine2"}
```

Juno (support): When stitched naively the payload contains a raw newline in the middle of an escape sequence and their JSON parser errors. They also saw a separate case where a non-BMP emoji was split across chunks (�.../\uDD1) and caused a surrogate pair error.

Maya K (support): Customer also flagged billing: they were charged for ~300 tokens for the call even though their app dropped the response due to parse error. Can we confirm if partial streamed tokens are billed when json_mode returns invalid JSON? cc @Samir

Samir (eng-runtime): thanks — can you paste the raw stream capture (exact bytes) and the request-id? need to check our chunk-stitching and escaping behavior. quick theory: if a chunk ends with a trailing backslash or a high-surrogate half, and we don't ensure token-level framing, the concatenated byte stream could produce an invalid escape.

Juno (support): request-id tr-ACME-9876, raw capture attached (pasted below):

-- RAW STREAM --
data: {"event":"response","chunk":"{\"id\":123,\"path\":\"C:\\\\Users\\\\alice\\\\Docu\"}\n"}
data: {"event":"response","chunk":"ments\\\\notes":\"She said: \"Hi\"\n\"}

Juno (support): you can see the first chunk ends with a backslash-escaped sequence and the next chunk starts with text that should continue the escape. The concatenation is valid only if the boundary is stitched correctly — their parser sees an invalid escape at the boundary.

Samir (eng-runtime): reproduction plan:
- run a streaming request with a tiny max_tokens (e.g., 8) so we force multiple chunks.
- enable json_mode / structured output.
- compare the byte-level chunks (not just printed strings).

Samir (eng-runtime): example curl to reproduce quickly:
```bash
curl -s -N https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-instruct-1\",\"stream\":true,\"max_tokens\":8,\"json_mode\":true,\"prompt\":\"emit a JSON object with a path and notes, and include an emoji: 🧑‍🔬\"}'
```

Samir (eng-runtime): if we can repro locally i'll instrument the runtime to log chunk boundaries and whether we cut inside an escape (e.g., trailing backslash or high surrogate). Also will check if our streaming serializer emits escapes as raw bytes or uses an incremental encoder that could drop a leading backslash on boundary.

logs-bot: trace_id=tr-ACME-9876  timestamp=2027-06-01T12:33:21Z  error=JSON::ParserError("Unterminated string at byte 248")  http_status=200  model=redwood-instruct-1

Maya K (support): Customer is blocked in production. Temporary workaround requested — should we advise them to set stream=false for now or buffer the stream until closing token? They prefer a fix but need a mitigation quickly.

Eve (eng-security): FYI if they buffer client-side make sure they validate auth and streaming timeouts; long buffering might surface stale tokens. 

Samir (eng-runtime): short-term mitigation: advise customer to set "stream": false or to buffer+validate full message before parsing. I'll prioritize a patch to ensure our streaming emitter never splits escape sequences or surrogate halves across chunks; if that's non-trivial we'll add an explicit chunk-boundary marker in the stream meta so clients can stitch deterministically.

Samir (eng-runtime): next steps: I will try to reproduce with the curl above, attach a minimal harness, and open an internal bug (BUG-rt-4532). I'll update this thread with a repro script + unit test. If anyone from support has the exact raw bytes file, please DM me the capture.

Maya K (support): forwarding mitigation to customer now, will ask for raw bytes. thanks. :thumbsup:

Juno (support): marking as escalated to eng-runtime. keeping the thread open until we have a fix or clear mitigation.

Maya K (support): note for billing team — please check charge window for tr-ACME-9876, customer disputes charge; i'll open a billing ticket after we confirm token accounting behavior.

Samir (eng-runtime): ack, will check token_metering logs once I repro.

logs-bot: billing_event: request_id=tr-ACME-9876 billed_tokens=312 billed_amount=$0.62

Maya K (support): thanks — adding billing ticket #BILL-1120.

Eve (eng-security): adding opt-in log redaction reminder when sharing raw captures outside company.

Juno (support): any updates post-repro?

Samir (eng-runtime): started a local run, reproduced the boundary-split on our incremental JSON encoder. Patch in progress to buffer last 2 bytes of a chunk if they could be part of an escape / surrogate. Will post PR and a test that simulates chunked backslash and split surrogate cases. ETA ~ EOD tomorrow.

Maya K (support): perfect — i'll relay ETA to customer and pause billing dispute until we have repro + mitigation. :pray:

Samir (eng-runtime): thanks — keeping this thread updated.
